title: eMudhra intermediate CA key compromise
summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs (plus their Sectigo cross-signs) can be recovered from the certificates. Browsers blocked them on 17-20 Oct 2026; clients that use a plain CA bundle without revocation checks keep trusting them until the affected roots are removed.

macos-system: macOS blocks the intermediates for apps that use Apple's frameworks, but the built-in curl, git, python3, perl, ruby and openssl read /etc/ssl/cert.pem without checking revocation. Apple has said it will update that file in a future macOS update. Until then, back up the file:
Remove emSign ECC Root CA - G3. This prints nothing on success:

t=$(mktemp) && awk -v s='=== /C=IN/OU=emSign PKI/O=eMudhra Technologies Limited/CN=emSign ECC Root CA - G3' '/^(===|###) /{skip=0} $0==s{skip=1} !skip' /etc/ssl/cert.pem > "$t" && [ -s "$t" ] && sudo install -m 0644 -o root -g wheel "$t" /etc/ssl/cert.pem; rm -f "$t"

That does not block the six Sectigo cross-signed intermediates, which chain to AAA Certificate Services. To block those too, also remove that root. This may break unaffected websites that still chain to it:

t=$(mktemp) && awk -v s='=== /C=GB/ST=Greater Manchester/L=Salford/O=Comodo CA Limited/CN=AAA Certificate Services' '/^(===|###) /{skip=0} $0==s{skip=1} !skip' /etc/ssl/cert.pem > "$t" && [ -s "$t" ] && sudo install -m 0644 -o root -g wheel "$t" /etc/ssl/cert.pem; rm -f "$t"
Check the result. It prints nothing once both roots are gone; if it shows an error, restore the backup:
openssl crl2pkcs7 -nocrl -certfile /etc/ssl/cert.pem | openssl pkcs7 -print_certs -noout | grep -E 'emSign ECC Root CA - G3|AAA Certificate Services'
A macOS update may replace /etc/ssl/cert.pem before Apple ships its fix, so repeat these steps after each update.
macos-pip: The built-in pip3 (and venvs made from the built-in python3) use their own outdated roots. Point them at the fixed system file:

F="$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_path("stdlib"))')/sitecustomize.py" && echo 'import os; os.environ.setdefault("PIP_CERT", "/etc/ssl/cert.pem")' | sudo tee -a "$F" > /dev/null && sudo chmod 644 "$F"
debian: Upgrade ca-certificates (apt-get update && apt-get install --only-upgrade ca-certificates). Until a fixed package is available, experts can distrust the roots:
If you use OpenJDK from Debian or Ubuntu packages, its keystore at /etc/ssl/certs/java/cacerts is not refreshed when the system store changes, after either step above. Recreate it as root:
alpine: Upgrade ca-certificates (apk upgrade ca-certificates). Until then:
fedora: Upgrade ca-certificates (dnf upgrade ca-certificates). Until then:

d=/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/blocklist; [ -d $d ] || d=/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/blacklist; trust extract --overwrite --format=pem-bundle --filter='pkcs11:object=Comodo%20AAA%20Services%20root;type=cert' $d/Comodo_AAA_Services_root.pem && trust extract --overwrite --format=pem-bundle --filter='pkcs11:object=emSign%20ECC%20Root%20CA%20-%20G3;type=cert' $d/emSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_G3.pem && update-ca-trust
suse: Upgrade ca-certificates-mozilla (zypper update ca-certificates-mozilla). Until then:

d=/etc/pki/trust/blocklist; [ -d $d ] || d=/etc/pki/trust/blacklist; trust extract --format=pem-bundle --filter='pkcs11:object=Comodo%20AAA%20Services%20root;type=cert' $d/Comodo_AAA_Services_root.pem && trust extract --format=pem-bundle --filter='pkcs11:object=emSign%20ECC%20Root%20CA%20-%20G3;type=cert' $d/emSign_ECC_Root_CA_-_G3.pem && update-ca-certificates
nixos: Add to your NixOS configuration and rebuild:
security.pki.caCertificateBlacklist = [ "Comodo AAA Services root" "emSign ECC Root CA - G3" ];
certifi: pip install --upgrade certifi  (or bump certifi in your lockfile)
pip: Upgrade pip, which vendors its own certifi copy: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
node: Upgrade Node.js; its root store is compiled into the binary.
java: Upgrade the JDK/JRE; cacerts ships with it. A JDK may also block certificates with its own distrust list, so confirm the version.
For OpenJDK from Debian or Ubuntu packages, recreate the keystore after updating ca-certificates:
generic: Replace this bundle with a current one (for example https://curl.se/ca/cacert.pem), or remove the affected roots listed above.
embedded: Upgrade this program to a patched release; its root store is compiled into the binary.
macos-verifier: Apple blocks these certificates through its own revocation data. Install pending macOS updates (softwareupdate -l) and re-run; if a chain is still accepted, apps that do not enforce Certificate Transparency remain exposed.
windows: Microsoft ships blocks through automatic certificate trust list updates. On machines that do not receive them, the tracker publishes Block-EmudhraCompromisedCA.ps1, which adds the 16 certificates to LocalMachine\Disallowed. On company-managed devices, ask IT before applying local changes:
